title: Rah ruuh — plans and the future
goal: Talk about what's going to happen, make plans, and remember the rule learners break most: after رَح, the b- prefix has to go.
bekal: state plans with رَح and negate them with مِش
tell apart رَح · بَدِّي, and the active participle for the future
make plans with clear time words

dialogs.title: حَكِي — خُطَّة لَلْعُطْلَة
dialogs.intro: Thursday afternoon. Samer, Laila, and Budi are making plans for the long weekend.

lines.speaker: سَامِر:
lines.id: What are you all doing over the holiday?

lines.speaker: لَيْلَى:
lines.text: أَنَا رَح رُوح عَ حَلَب. عِنْدِي عِيلِة هْنِيك.
lines.id: I'm going to Aleppo. My family's there.
lines.literal: I will I-go to Aleppo. at-me family there.

lines.speaker: سَامِر:
lines.text: تَعَال مَعِي. رَح نِطْلَع عَ الْبَحِر.
lines.id: Come with me. We're going to the beach.
lines.literal: come with-me. will we-go-out to the-sea.

lines.speaker: سَامِر:
lines.id: Friday morning. We'll be back Sunday.

lines.speaker: سَامِر:
lines.text: عِنْد خَالِي. عِنْدُو بَيْت قَرِيب مِن الشَّطّ.
lines.id: At my uncle's. His house is near the beach.
lines.literal: at uncle-my. at-him house near from the-beach.

lines.speaker: لَيْلَى:
lines.text: يَا رَيْتْنِي مَعْكُن! بَسّ مِش رَح إِقْدَر.
lines.baca: ya rētni ma‘kun! bass mish rah i’dar.
lines.id: Oh, I wish I could come! But I won't be able to.
lines.literal: oh if-only-I with-you-all! but not will I-can.

lines.speaker: سَامِر:
lines.id: Budi, what are you taking with you?

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.text: شْوَي تْيَاب وْكَامِيرَا. مِش رَح آخُد كْتِير.
lines.baca: shway tyaab w kaamiira. mish rah aakhud ktiir.
lines.id: A few clothes and a camera. I won't take much.
lines.literal: few clothes and camera. not will I-take much.

lines.speaker: سَامِر:
lines.text: مْنِيح. رَح إِمُرّ عَلَيْك السَّاعَة سَبْعَة.
lines.id: Great. I'll pick you up at seven.
lines.literal: great. will I-pass by-you hour seven.

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.text: رَح كُون جَاهِز. مَا رَح إِتْأَخَّر.
lines.baca: rah kuun jaahiz. ma rah it’akhkhar.
lines.id: I'll be ready. I won't be late.
lines.literal: will I-be ready. not will I-be-late.

lines.speaker: لَيْلَى:
lines.id: Have a safe trip. Send me photos!

notes: **⚠️ After رَح, the b- prefix drops.** "I go" is بْرُوح, but "I'm going to go" is رَح رُوح — no b. It's the same rule as after بَدِّي in unit 7, and it's the one learners break most. رَح بْرُوح sounds wrong right away.

**The negative is مِش, not مَا.** The form is مِش رَح رُوح ("I'm not going to go"). It's an exception to memorize: even though it sounds like you're negating the verb, what's actually negated is رَح. You'll also hear مَا رَح in Jordan, and it isn't wrong.
**There's a very common short form: حَـ.** حَرُوح means the same as رَح رُوح, just faster. In Lebanon it's more common than the long form. As a beginner, use رَح, because it's easier to hear.

**The difference between رَح and بَدِّي is intention versus plan.** بَدِّي رُوح means "I want to go" — a wish that may not happen. رَح رُوح means "I'm going to go" — already decided. English "I wanna" and "I'm gonna" are close cousins here, so keep them apart.

**The phrase يَا رَيْت means "if only."** It's used for wishes that can't come true, and it takes endings: يَا رَيْتْنِي ("if only I"), يَا رَيْتَك ("if only you"). You'll hear it a lot, always with a slightly wistful tone.
**The phrase اَلْمَرَّة الْجَايِة means "next time."** It's the gentlest way to turn down an invitation you can't accept, and it's almost always followed by إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه.

grammars.title: The future with رَح and the bare form
after: There's really just one rule: **drop the b, leave the rest.** بِتْرُوح becomes تْرُوح · بِيرُوح becomes يْرُوح · مِنْرُوح becomes نْرُوح. If you've learned the table in unit 8, this one comes free.
The word رَح itself never changes across the eight persons, just like عَم in unit 8. It's one fixed word you simply put in front.

grammars.title: Three ways to talk about the future
after: The participle (رَايِح، جَايِ، مْسَافِر) is used for near plans that are already fixed, just like English "I'm leaving tomorrow." It feels livelier than رَح, and native speakers choose it very often.
⚠️ Keep the two negatives in the last two rows apart. مِش رَح رُوح is a fact ("it just won't happen"); مَا بَدِّي رُوح is a choice ("I refuse"). Mixing them up can sound rude.

blocks.text: The word الْجَايِ means "the coming one" and is used for every "next" unit of time. Its form follows the gender of the noun: اَلْأُسْبُوع الْجَايِ (masculine) but اَلسِّنِة الْجَايِة (feminine). The same pattern applies to الْمَاضِي ("the last one").

blocks.title: ⚠️ What إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه really means
items: Said about your own plans, it means "God willing" — an acknowledgment that it isn't up to you.
Said **in reply to an invitation**, it often means "maybe, but don't count on it." It's a gentle way of saying no that embarrasses nobody.
If you need a firm answer, ask again directly: يَعْنِي أَكِيد رَح تِيجِي؟ People in the Levant will answer honestly and won't think you're rude.

blocks.text: The phrase خَلِّينَا نْشُوف means "we'll see," and works just like it does in English: it puts off a decision without saying no. خَلِّي on its own means "let," and it also forms suggestions: خَلِّينَا نْرُوح ("let's go").

blocks.title: Three ways to invite
items: Most direct: يَلَّا نْرُوح *yalla nruuh* ("let's go").
Most polite: شُو رَأْيَك نْرُوح…؟ *shu ra’yak nruuh…?* ("how about we go…?").
Warmest: تَعَال مَعْنَا *ta‘aal ma‘na* ("come with us") — and turning it down needs a reason, because it's an invitation, not just a suggestion.
What are you (f.) going to bring?
How about we go to the beach?

exercises.prompt: Change into the correct رَح form (drop the b- prefix).

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.

answers: بُكْرَا رَح رُوح عَ الشَّام. — رَح نِرْجَع يَوْم الْأَحَد. — شُو رَح تَاخْدِي؟ — مِش رَح إِتْأَخَّر. — شُو رَأْيَك نْرُوح عَ الْبَحِر؟ — اَلْمَرَّة الْجَايِة إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه.
رَح رُوح عَ السُّوق — رَح يِدْرُس بُكْرَا — رَح نِرْجَع الْأَحَد — رَح تَاكْلِي مَعْنَا — رَح يِجُوا الْأُسْبُوع الْجَايِ — رَح تْنَامُوا عِنْد خَالَك
رَح — بَدِّي — مِش رَح — رَح — بَدِّي — مِش رَح
بُكْرَا رَح رُوح عَ الشَّام. — شُو رَح تَعْمُل؟ — مِش رَح إِقْدَر. — شُو رَأْيَك نْرُوح عَ الْبَحِر؟ — اَلْمَرَّة الْجَايِة إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه. — رَح كُون جَاهِز.
